**Near the horizon:** short Earth chord.

**Downward:** atmospheric-muon rejection.

$A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ includes interaction, propagation and event selection.

### What energy is measured?

| Event | Light constrains | Parent-neutrino inference |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Contained $\nu_e$ CC | Electromagnetic + hadronic deposits | $E_{\mathrm{dep}}\simeq E_\nu$, after response calibration |
| Through-going $\mu$ | Muon energy losses inside the array | $E_\mu$ at the detector, then a spectrum-dependent $E_\nu$ distribution |
| Neutral current | Hadronic deposit | $E_{\mathrm{dep}}\sim yE_\nu$; outgoing neutrino is unseen |

**Historical HESE reconstruction (2013):** tracks $<1^\circ$; cascades $10–15^\circ$.

Quoted median angular scales above about $50\,\mathrm{TeV}$. Neutrino–muon kinematics adds a separate spread.

::: {.media-caption}
$y$: inelasticity · [IceCube reconstruction (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238v2)
:::

::::::

::: {.notes}
Spend about 90 seconds on Effective area. Read the three curves as consequences
of the Earth and background cuts already discussed. The published review curve
is illustrative; it is not a current detector-performance comparison. Theta
is detector zenith, 0 degrees downward and 180 upward. The response depends
on event selection as well as instrument geometry. Through-going tracks can
originate outside the instrumented volume.

T is live time, Phi a differential incident intensity per solid angle, and alpha
indexes the included flavour/sign components. A_eff has area units and already
includes neutrino interaction, attenuation and analysis efficiency. Do not
multiply it by another cross section or Earth transmission. An evolving array
requires time-dependent exposure, or the corresponding season sum. A point
source uses a directional flux rather than an isotropic per-steradian intensity.

Starting events is an optional historical response example for the discovery
sample. The source shows an all-sky average, with neutrino/antineutrino conventions
defined in the paper; its high-energy electron-flavour peak includes the Glashow
resonance. It must not be used for today's through-going-track exposure.

The energy table is qualitative. Visible energy and true neutrino energy need
a response distribution, including inelasticity, escaping particles, stochastic
muon losses and detector calibration. Cascade electromagnetic-equivalent energy
is not identical to every hadronic deposit. Tau decays can carry invisible energy.
Angular reconstruction of the secondary and neutrino–muon kinematics are
distinct contributions. The quoted angular scales describe historical HESE reconstruction, not current
performance or a matched detector ranking. A flux fit forward-predicts each
reconstructed bin using an energy-response distribution and background model;
it does not identify each reconstructed energy with true neutrino energy.

Both effective-area graphs are lecture-style redraws of curves digitized from
the published figures (vector histogram for HESE; raster tracing for the review's
illustrative curves, accurate to about 0.01 dex). Quantities, binning and axis
ranges are unchanged. Method and tests: `assets/response/README.md`.

Sources: [IceCube HESE response](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238v2),
[AMANDA reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0407044),
[Spiering, sections 3.1.3–3.1.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::
